description.value: The study examined whether individual differences in trait reward drive predict neural responses to images of food in healthy participants using functional magnetic resonance imaging.

spans.text: Using functional magnetic resonance imaging, we report that individual variation in trait reward sensitivity (as measured by the Behavioral Activation Scale) is highly correlated with activation to images of appetizing foods

source_definition.value: Stimulus condition category comprising appetizing, disgusting, bland, and nonfood images; condition effects and contrasts were estimated from passive-viewing blocks.

spans.text: During scanning, participants passively viewed full color photographs of foods consistently identified as highly appetizing (e.g., chocolate cake, ice cream sundae), disgusting (e.g., rotten meat, moldy bread), or bland (e.g., uncooked rice, potatoes), and similar photographs of nonfood objects (e.g., videocassette, iron).

model_settings.value: SPM99 random-effects group analysis; participant-level condition effects were estimated with boxcar regressors convolved with a canonical hemodynamic response function in a general linear model, with spatial realignment parameters as regressors, high-pass filtering for low-frequency drift, and low-pass filtering with the canonical hemodynamic response function.

spans.text: EPI images were corrected for slice timing and head movement, and undistortion based on field strength derived from a phase map was applied ( Cusack et al., 2003 ).
